Answer: C
Reason: Dysphonia in the context of tracheal or mediastinal malignancy is often caused by compression or invasion of the recurrent laryngeal nerve, which courses through the aortopulmonary window near the left hilum; enlargement of the left hilum on chest X-ray would correlate with this pathology. The provided axial CT image confirms a mass in the anterior mediastinum/aortopulmonary window region adjacent to the trachea, consistent with left hilar/mediastinal involvement.
